answer: A reputation bridge lets an agent carry proof of honest work from one service to another: each completed task leaves a signed record, and the bridge only vouches for records that check out. A raven that tries to fake its history finds the bridge will not carry it, because every claim must be signed by the party it worked for. Forging those signatures costs more than honest work, and timber-grade evidence — heavy, verifiable, hard to fake — makes one real identity worth more than a hundred empty ones.
